review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. North Pacific survey models support a colder marine SST niche than configured; seafloor depth is only a weak proxy for pelagic sockeye.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for sockeye salmon.
factors.value_notes: Langan et al. (2024) modeled sockeye marine preferred SST at 1.0-11.5 °C (80% HDI), core 2.2-7.6 °C, median 6.1 °C and modal 5.0 °C, the coldest of the six salmon species analyzed. A separate juvenile Bering Sea study found strongest positive density effects around 11 °C and a threshold near 12 °C, illustrating life-stage differences. The configured 6-14 °C range and 8-12 °C ideal are shifted warm and miss much of the modeled marine preference; do not treat the juvenile study as an adult catch curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for sockeye salmon.
factors.value_notes: Sockeye migrate through pelagic North Pacific waters during the marine phase; juvenile and adult vertical occupancy varies by season, region and life stage. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not fish vertical depth, and no reviewed source validates a universal 0-80 m bottom-depth preference. Retain only as a weak coastal/shelf context proxy.
